coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across foundational and current scholarship on graph layout algorithms covering force-directed (Eades 1984, Fruchterman-Reingold 1991), hierarchical/layered (Sugiyama 1981), tree layouts (Reingold-Tilford), orthogonal/octilinear, and emerging techniques. Sources span three decades from seminal papers through contemporary research. Included: peer-reviewed publications (IEEE TVCG, ACM, Springer, ScienceDirect), foundational texts (Di Battista, Tamassia, Munzner), design theory (Shneiderman, Tufte, Norman, Pirolli), survey papers from IEEE and ACM, arXiv preprints on recent advances (GNNs, accessibility, dynamic graphs), and canonical implementations (Graphviz, OGDF, yFiles, D3.js). Deduplication applied across direct papers, handbook chapters, and derivative works. Coverage includes both theoretical foundations (planarity, crossing minimization, spectral methods) and HCI aspects (aesthetic criteria, user studies, interaction). Notable gaps: some paywalled conference proceedings and proprietary research reports marked as reference-only.

sources.title: Graph drawing by force-directed placement
sources.notes: Seminal paper on force-directed graph layout. Fruchterman & Reingold introduce modification of spring-embedder model for undirected graphs with straight edges, striving for uniform edge lengths using physical force analogies. Core algorithm: attractive forces between adjacent nodes, repulsive forces between all nodes. Foundational for modern force-directed layout implementations.

sources.title: A heuristic for graph drawing
sources.notes: Peter Eades' 1984 foundational work introducing spring-embedder model for graph visualization. Models graph as mechanical system with steel rings (vertices) and springs (edges). Uses logarithmic force functions to handle long-range repulsion. Targets graphs up to 30 vertices, designed for aesthetic layouts with uniform edge length and symmetry.

sources.title: Methods for visual understanding of hierarchical system structures
sources.notes: Sugiyama, Tagawa & Toda (1981) introduce foundational framework for layered/hierarchical graph drawing. Five-phase approach: cycle removal, layer assignment, crossing minimization, coordinate assignment, edge routing. Establishes methodology still widely used in tools like Graphviz, yWorks, and OGDF.

sources.title: Graph Drawing: Algorithms for the Visualization of Graphs
sources.notes: Comprehensive textbook by Di Battista, Eades, Tamassia & Tollis covering fundamental algorithmic techniques for graph drawing. Seminal reference work describing force-directed, hierarchical, tree, and orthogonal layout algorithms with mathematical foundations and practical considerations.

sources.title: Handbook of Graph Drawing and Visualization
sources.notes: Authoritative handbook edited by Roberto Tamassia (2013) covering state-of-the-art in graph drawing and visualization. Chapters by leading researchers cover planar/orthogonal drawing, force-directed algorithms, hierarchical layouts, labeling, and emerging techniques. Industry-standard reference.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Tamara Munzner's comprehensive textbook (2014, AK Peters/CRC) on information visualization fundamentals. Introduces nested model for visualization design, mark-channel theory, effectiveness principles, and application to graph layouts. Widely adopted in academic courses worldwide.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (2nd Edition)
sources.notes: Edward Tufte's seminal work on statistical graphics and data visualization principles. Introduces data-ink ratio, identifies chartjunk, analyzes graph design history, and establishes aesthetic standards for visual representation. Foundational for understanding visualization design criteria applicable to graph layouts.

sources.title: The Eyes Have It: A Task by Data Type Taxonomy for Information Visualizations
sources.notes: Ben Shneiderman's foundational paper introducing visualization mantra (overview, zoom, filter, details-on-demand) and task taxonomy. Established treemaps and principles for hierarchical visualization. Defined emerging field of information visualization with focus on interactive exploration.

sources.title: Force-Directed Drawing Algorithms
sources.notes: Stephen Kobourov's comprehensive chapter in Graph Drawing Handbook covering force-directed algorithms. Reviews Eades, Fruchterman-Reingold, and modern variants. Discusses convergence properties, parameterization, and practical considerations for implementation in visualization systems.

sources.title: Planar Orthogonal and Polyline Drawing Algorithms
sources.notes: Christian Duncan's handbook chapter on orthogonal and polyline drawing. Covers planar orthogonal drawings (edges horizontal/vertical only), topology-shape-metrics approach, Fry's algorithm, and applications to UML diagrams and circuit layouts.

sources.title: Force-Directed Edge Bundling for Graph Visualization
sources.notes: Danny Holten's 2009 paper introducing force-directed edge bundling technique for reducing visual clutter in dense graphs. Bundles edges using forces while maintaining visibility. Widely adopted for large network visualization and hierarchical edge bundling variant.

sources.title: Edge Crossing Minimization in Graphs - A Survey
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of crossing minimization algorithms - a fundamental NP-hard problem in graph drawing. Covers exact algorithms, heuristics (barycenter method), and parameterized complexity approaches for various graph classes.

sources.title: Graph drawing and information visualization
sources.notes: ACM Computing Surveys paper by Di Battista et al. covering graph drawing algorithms and visualization techniques. Surveys force-directed, hierarchical, orthogonal layouts and crossing minimization. Seminal survey for comprehensive overview of the field.

sources.title: Information Foraging: A Theory of How People Navigate on the Web
sources.notes: Peter Pirolli and Stuart Card's foundational work on information foraging theory. Explains how users navigate information spaces through information scent - applying animal foraging behavior to visualization and web navigation. Critical for understanding graph visualization interaction patterns.

sources.title: Principles of Human-Centered Design
sources.notes: Don Norman's human-centered design principles foundational for visualization UX. Emphasizes understanding users, iteration, and alignment with human psychology. Applicable to layout algorithm selection, parameter tuning, and interactive exploration of graph visualizations.

sources.title: A better heuristic for orthogonal graph drawings
sources.notes: Carsten Gutwenger's work on improved heuristics for orthogonal graph drawing. Refines topology-shape-metrics approach for practical large-graph layout with emphasis on minimizing bends and area.

sources.title: Drawing Graphviz Edge Splines
sources.notes: Technical explanation of spline-based edge routing in Graphviz. Covers Bezier curves for edge drawing, control point generation, and practical implementation for smoother edge rendering than straight lines in orthogonal/octilinear layouts.

sources.title: Comparative Evaluation of Bipartite, Node-Link, and Matrix-Based Network Representations
sources.notes: Empirical user study comparing node-link diagrams, matrices, and bipartite layouts for network visualization. Evaluates effectiveness for different task types, providing evidence-based guidance for layout selection in different contexts.

sources.title: Node, Node-Link, and Node-Link-Group Diagrams: An Evaluation
sources.notes: Comparative evaluation of node-only, node-link, and node-link-group diagram representations. Controlled experiment with nine task categories showing node-link diagrams excel at connectivity tasks while adding groups doesn't hurt performance.

sources.title: A Taxonomy and Survey of Dynamic Graph Visualization
sources.notes: Survey of dynamic/temporal graph visualization distinguishing animation-based and timeline-based approaches. Reviews mental map preservation, layout stability, and techniques for handling time-varying network topology.

sources.title: Spectral layout
sources.notes: Overview of spectral graph layout methods using eigenvectors/eigenvalues of Laplacian or adjacency matrices. Explains Fiedler vector approach and advantages: optimal layouts computable rapidly without iterative convergence.

sources.title: Graph visualization at scale: strategies that work
sources.notes: Practitioner guide to large-scale graph visualization strategies. Covers layout algorithm performance bottlenecks, filtering/abstraction, interaction patterns, and tool capabilities (Gephi, Cytoscape, NetV.js) for graphs with thousands to millions of nodes/edges.

sources.title: Hierarchical edge bundling
sources.notes: Tutorial on hierarchical edge bundling (Holten's technique) for compound graphs with hierarchy and associations. Explains B-spline bundling for clutter reduction and practical implementation considerations.

sources.title: Constraint-Based Spring-Model Algorithm for Graph Layout
sources.notes: Kamps & Kleinz work on constraint-based spring embedder variants. Shows how to extend force-directed methods to enforce user-specified layout constraints (node position fixing, distance preservation) while maintaining energy minimization.

sources.title: Upward planar drawing
sources.notes: Overview of upward planar drawings for directed acyclic graphs - embeddings where edges are monotonic upward curves with no crossings. NP-complete in general; solvable in polynomial time with prescribed y-coordinates. Ideal for hierarchical layout.

sources.title: Graph planarity and path addition method of Hopcroft-Tarjan for planarity testing
sources.notes: Explanation of Hopcroft-Tarjan linear-time planarity testing algorithm (1974). Path-addition algorithm using DFS for O(n) planarity testing - foundational for determining which graphs admit planar drawing.

sources.title: The Reingold-Tilford graph layout algorithm
sources.notes: Reference for Reingold-Tilford tree layout algorithm (1981). Linear O(n) algorithm for tidy tree drawing with parents centered above children. Widely implemented in igraph, D3.js, and other libraries for hierarchical data.

sources.title: d3-force: Force simulations
sources.notes: D3.js force simulation module implementing velocity Verlet integration for force-directed layout. Standard practical implementation with configurable forces (charge, link, center, collision). Widely used for interactive web-based graph visualization.

sources.title: Graphviz - Graph Visualization Software
sources.notes: Industry-standard open-source graph visualization tool. Implements Sugiyama hierarchical layout, force-directed (via neato), and custom layouts. Core algorithms documented; widely used in academia and industry for automatic graph drawing.

sources.title: OGDF: The Open Graph Drawing Framework
sources.notes: Comprehensive C++ library implementing graph drawing and visualization algorithms. Covers force-directed, hierarchical, planar, orthogonal, and specialized layouts. Academic reference implementation for algorithm research and teaching.

sources.title: Guide to Creating Knowledge Graph Visualizations
sources.notes: yFiles commercial graph library documentation covering layout algorithms (force-directed, hierarchical, orthogonal, radial, tree). Professional-grade implementation with extensive algorithm customization and aesthetic options.

sources.title: igraph - Network Analysis and Visualization
sources.notes: igraph R/Python package implementing comprehensive graph layout algorithms including force-directed (Fruchterman-Reingold, Kamada-Kawai), tree, circular, and spectral layouts. Accessible implementation for data science applications.

sources.title: Structure-Aware Simplification for Hypergraph Visualization
sources.notes: Recent work on hypergraph visualization addressing scalability challenges. Proposes structure-aware simplification maintaining structural properties while reducing visual clutter - extends node-link paradigm to hyperedges.

sources.title: Metrics for Graph Drawing Aesthetics
sources.notes: Quantitative metrics for evaluating graph layout quality: edge crossings, bends, edge length variance, area, symmetry. Enables empirical comparison of layout algorithms and objective optimization criteria.

sources.title: Explainability in Graph Neural Networks: A Taxonomic Survey
sources.notes: Survey of explainability/interpretability methods for graph neural networks. Covers visualization approaches for understanding GNN decision-making and learned graph representations - emerging intersection of ML and graph visualization.

sources.title: Our Stories, Our Data: Co-designing Visualizations with People with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
sources.notes: User-centered research on accessible data visualization design. Demonstrates importance of inclusive design for graph visualization, ensuring color-blind-friendly palettes, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility.

sources.title: Graph Exploration with Embedding-Guided Layouts
sources.notes: Recent work combining graph embeddings (from neural networks) with layout algorithms to guide exploratory visualization. Bridges machine learning representations with traditional layout computation.

sources.title: Confluent Drawings: Visualizing Non-planar Diagrams in a Planar Way
sources.notes: Novel drawing style using edge bundling to achieve confluent (bundled) visualization of non-planar graphs. Edges bundled into paths, reducing visual clutter of edge crossings while maintaining readability.

sources.title: A Survey on the Visual Analytics of Knowledge Graph
sources.notes: Survey of visual analytics techniques for knowledge graphs. Covers schema-centered visualization, ontology visualization, and scalability challenges for large RDF/semantic graphs.

sources.title: Effective and Efficient PageRank-based Positioning for Graph Visualization
sources.notes: Uses PageRank centrality for initial node positioning in force-directed layouts, improving convergence and layout quality. Demonstrates integration of network analysis metrics with classical layout algorithms.

sources.title: HOTVis: Higher-Order Time-Aware Visualisation of Dynamic Graphs
sources.notes: Novel approach to temporal graph visualization capturing higher-order interactions. Extends layout algorithms to handle time-varying topology while preserving temporal coherence.
